title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Streamlining and Improving Economic Outcomes for Australians) Bill 2022
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Streamlining and Improving Economic Outcomes for Australians) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change licensing rules for overseas financial service providers, expand superannuation fund reporting duties and give small businesses additional options in tax disputes.
It would introduce licensing exemptions, apply corporate reporting and auditing rules to registrable superannuation entities, and allow temporary tribunal orders affecting disputed tax recovery.
Licensing changes would start on 1 April 2023, superannuation changes on 1 July 2023, and tax review changes would apply to applications after royal assent.
changes: Eligible overseas providers serving professional investors could operate without an Australian financial services licence, subject to conditions.
The minister could designate overseas regulators with comparable regulatory arrangements for the new exemptions.
Superannuation licensees would have to publish annual financial, directors' and auditors' reports on their funds' websites.
Small businesses could ask the Administrative Appeals Tribunal to pause specified tax decisions while it reviewed them.
summary.affected: Foreign financial services providers and the professional investors they serve, registrable superannuation entities, and small business entities seeking stays of tax decisions under review are affected.
